subject: Question about a misspecified multinomial model

messages.author: 4525396ad5bfc811
messages.subject: Question about a misspecified multinomial model
parts:
Hi Stan Board,

I have been trying to develop a model to estimate species abundances from ecological community data to answer questions about biodiversity. The data are a matrix of simulated species counts where rows are sites (e.g., quadrats, transects) and columns are individual species. For the prior on the multinomial thetas, I have been trying to use a softmax distribution. In constructing the model, I was a bit sloppy in my code and so some of the model was vectorized while other parts were not. The model (attached) ran very slowly (~5min for 100 iterations) but the posterior predictive check looked great. 

Here is the original model:
data {
  int<lower=1> nSpp; // no. of spp. (columns)
  int<lower=1> nObs; // no. of sites (rows)
  int<lower=0> obs[nObs,nSpp];
  int<lower=0> sizes[nObs]; // rowsums for posterior predictive check
}

parameters {  
  vector[nSpp] mu;
  real<lower=0> sigma;
  vector[nSpp] thetaRaw[nObs];
}

transformed parameters {
vector[nSpp] alpha[nObs];
simplex[nSpp] theta[nObs];
  for(n in 1:nObs) {
   for(s in 1:(nSpp)) {
   alpha[n,s] <- mu[s] + sigma .* thetaRaw[n,s];
  
   }
     theta[n] <- softmax(alpha[n]);
    }
}

model {
sigma ~ cauchy(0,2); 
  for(s in 1:nSpp){
   mu ~ normal(0,5);
  
  
   for(n in 1:nObs){
   thetaRaw[n,s] ~ normal(0,1);
     obs[n] ~ multinomial(theta[n]);
   }
  }
}
 
generated quantities {
  int<lower=0> yNew[nObs,nSpp];
  int<lower=0> yVec[nObs*nSpp];
 

// -----------------------------------------
   for(n in 1:nObs){
        yNew[n] <- multinomial_rng(theta[n],sizes[n]);
   }
  }
  // put matrix of new obs into a vector for easy post. pred. comparison
   yVec <- to_array_1d(yNew); 
}


When I cleaned up the code so that everything was vectorized, the model ran much faster but the ppcheck was a lot worse. I figured out that what I was doing was looping over the likelihood and one of the vectorized priors nSpp times accidentally. I was able to recreate this by writing:

increment_log_prob(nSpp*normal_log(mu, 0, 5));
increment_log_prob(nSpp*multinomial_log(obs[n],theta[n]));

I now realize that this is wrong, but my questions are two-fold:
1) Why did I get parameter estimates from this error that fit so well with my observed data? What exactly is going on here?
2) Is there a way to code this model properly that will give me equivalent results?


Thanks for any help you might have!

Best,
Zach Marion

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Question about a misspecified multinomial model
parts:
1. Replicating data will mainly cause less shrinkage toward the prior
and too-narrow posterior intervals. So if you check the calibration of
the interval coverage it'll be off.

2. You probably want to change this (reindented so I could read it):

for (s in 1:nSpp) {
mu ~ normal(0, 5);
for (n in 1:nObs) {

to this, which doesn't have the redundancy:

mu ~ normal(0, 5);
to_vector(thetaRaw) ~ normal(0, 1);
for (n in 1:nObs)

This requires thetaRaw being declared as matrix[nObs, nSpp],
which may require some other type fiddling because now [nObs]
returns a rwo vector.

And you probably want to make alpha and theta local variables in
the model (where you have to declare it as a simple vector as
there are no constraints). That way it won't get saved every iteration.

- Bob

P.S. Never ever ever use tabs in code! They display differently
in different contexts.
